people.role: Head of Vọng Triều Đường; keeper of the lamp chain and the sea-wards of the gulf coast
people.appearance: A tall, salt-greyed man who never sits with his back to the sea and carries a lit bronze storm lamp even at noon.
people.backstory: Ôn Thủ Đăng was born in 860 at Âu Lộ Thôn, where the pearl divers of burned Châu Lệ Cảng settled and never dived again (A259). The hall's founder Cơ Châu Lệ (co_chau_le) took him at twelve. He has kept its lamps for three hundred years: a chain of towers along the gulf coast, lit every night so that any sail is seen and passed from tower to tower to the palace fleet at Thạch Cơ Thành. No pirate has come since the Purge (C153). He has watched an empty sea for four centuries and will not let a lamp go out. He drinks with the palace admiral Phàn Vọng Hải (phan_vong_hai), who comes from the same pearl-diver stock, and calls his diving for the lost sabre a waste of good summers. In 914 he wrote the Last Lamp Vigil and has never said why that winter. In 1190 the palace asked the hall to ward the Thạch Cơ jetty against storms; he said the hall watches for sails.
people.wants: Every tower in the chain lit again: three have been dark for want of keepers.
people.secret: In 913 he was keeper of the Kim Sa lamp. On the festival night he asked his sworn brother Dịch Thủy Thanh (dich_thuy_thanh) to keep it while he went to a girl in Lam Điện. The storm tide came that night, Kim Sa Trấn drowned (V171), and Dịch drowned at the lamp. Ôn has kept every lamp lit since then because of that one night, and he refuses storm wards because a storm took Dịch.

people.role: Elder of the storm wards; wants the hall to stop watching for pirates and wall the coast against the sea
people.appearance: A square-shouldered woman in a salt-stiff coat, who measures every wall she passes with her eyes.
people.backstory: Chân Định Lan grew up in Hải Mục Thôn, where the sea pastures flood in the autumn storms, and joined the hall because it was the only sect on the coast that knew wards. She learned them from Ôn Thủ Đăng (on_thu_dang) and has argued with him for a century. No pirate has come in four hundred years. Storm tides drowned Kim Sa Trấn (V171) and cracked the palace's jetty at Thạch Cơ Thành (A312). She wants the lamp oil spent on breakwater arrays. In 1190, when Ôn refused the palace's request to ward the jetty, she went to Thạch Cơ alone at night and laid what she could. The storm cracked it anyway. The palace rebuilt it with Xích Thành stone, and she has not forgiven herself.
people.wants: A breakwater array along the gulf, paid for with the lamps' oil, before the next storm tide.
people.secret: She has written to the palace admiral Phàn Vọng Hải (phan_vong_hai), asking him to persuade the palace to order the hall to the sea-walls over Ôn's head.

people.role: Keeper of the northern lamp in the crumbling fort of Liệu Phàm Bảo
people.appearance: A gaunt man in a seal-skin coat whose eyes have gone pale from staring at the dark sea.
people.backstory: A Sunrise Village fisher's son who has kept the lamp in Liệu Phàm Bảo alone since 1150. The palace withdrew the fort's garrison in 790 (V140), the year the hall was founded, and the hall has kept a lamp in its tower ever since. Twice last winter he saw sails pass south at night with no lamp lit. He wrote to Ôn Thủ Đăng (on_thu_dang), and no one has answered.

people.role: Steward of the hall: lamp oil, salt and laver, and the accounts
people.appearance: A brisk woman with salt-cracked hands and an abacus at her belt.
people.backstory: Her people at Hàm Trạch are the grandchildren of Hải Diêm Trấn's salt makers, burned out by Thôn Hải in 764 (V139). She keeps the hall's money, which is salt, laver and a small palace stipend, and spends most of it on lamp oil. She has shown Chân Định Lan (chan_dinh_lan) that the oil for one year would build a furlong of breakwater.

people.backstory: A pearl diver of Châu Lệ Cảng who was twenty-two when Thôn Hải burned the harbour in 762 (C151) and changed her name to its name. After the Purge she gathered the survivors of the pirate years by the burned piers and swore them to an oath: no harbour on this coast will burn again (V141). She wrote the Lamp-Ward Seal Canon and taught Ôn Thủ Đăng (on_thu_dang).

people.role: Ôn Thủ Đăng's sworn brother; drowned keeping the Kim Sa lamp
people.backstory: An Âu Lộ boy who swore brotherhood with Ôn Thủ Đăng (on_thu_dang) on the founder's tower. On the festival night of 913 he kept Ôn's lamp at Kim Sa Trấn so that Ôn could go to a girl in Lam Điện. The storm tide came that night and drowned the town (V171), and he drowned at the lamp with it still lit.
